The productive window ends at 17:00, so even the high case leaves under 1 h of loading.

input.title: Move LH-11 from TP-1250-02 to TP-1310-04 to cover the failed LH-07

options.description: No reaction. TP-1310-04 (8.4 g/t) has no loader from 09:30 to 17:00 (7.5 h), because LH-07 is unreliable and nothing is planned for it.
Hold until LH-07 is repaired (PR-0001 likely 14:30, 5 h). TP-1310-04 loses 09:30-14:30. A high case of 16:00 would lose 6.5 h (195 t, 52.7 oz).

Move LH-11 (TP-1250-02, 4.1 g/t, phase carguio, the lowest-grade loading-only stope) to TP-1310-04. The move takes 1 h across levels, so loading starts about 10:30. TP-1310-04 loses 1 h (30 t, 8.1 oz). TP-1250-02 loses 150 t, 19.8 oz from 09:30 to 17:00.

input.calculation: Formula: oz = t x g/31.1035. The productive window is 07:00-17:00 (10 h). TP-1310-04 plan is 300 t / 10 h = 30 t/h; at 8.4 g/t that is 8.10 oz/h. The failure was at 09:18 and the repair clock starts about 09:30. Do nothing: 7.5 h x 30 = 225 t, 60.8 oz. Wait for repair: 5 h x 30 = 150 t, 40.5 oz (PR-0001 likely back 14:30). Reassign: rules LOADER-BACKUP-01/02 say to take the loader from the lowest-grade stope that is in phase carguio only. TP-1220-01 (3.9 g/t) is carguio-perforacion and so excluded. The lowest-grade carguio stope is TP-1250-02 (4.1 g/t, LH-11). Rule MOVE-TIME-01 gives 1 h for a ramp move from level 1250 to 1310, so loading starts about 10:30. Protected at TP-1310-04 is 6.5 h x 30 = 195 t = 52.7 oz, relative to do nothing. Lost at TP-1250-02 is 7.5 h x 20 t/h (200 t / 10 h) = 150 t x 4.1 / 31.1035 = 19.8 oz. Net is 52.7 - 19.8 = 32.9 oz. Total at risk is (1 h x 30 = 30 t, 8.1 oz) + (150 t, 19.8 oz) = 180 t, 27.9 oz, against 40.5 oz for waiting. Reassigning is the best option, and it also protects against the high repair case. Alternatives were worse: TP-1310-11 (LH-10, same level, 0.5 h) is 6.0 g/t and loses more ounces, and it is not the lowest grade, so it breaks LOADER-BACKUP-01. Option to refine: if LH-07 is back at 14:30, LH-11 could return to 1250-02, which takes 1 h and gives about 1.5 h of loading (about 30 t, 4 oz). I did not assume this because LH-07 is chronically unreliable.

content.text:
I submitted proposal PR-0002 for approval. It moves LH-11 from TP-1250-02 to TP-1310-04, the high-grade stope that lost its loader when LH-07 failed.

- **Why LH-11:** TP-1250-02 is the lowest-grade stope (4.1 g/t) that is loading only, so it can give up its loader under rules LOADER-BACKUP-01 and -02. TP-1220-01 is lower grade but runs drilling and loading together, so it keeps its loader.
- **Timing:** The ramp move takes about 1 h, so loading at TP-1310-04 starts around 10:30.
- **Net effect:** It protects 195 t and 52.7 oz at TP-1310-04. It costs 150 t and 19.8 oz at TP-1250-02, a net gain of 32.9 oz.
- **Total at risk:**

| Option | Tonnes at risk | Oz at risk |
|---|---|---|
| Do nothing | 225 | 60.8 |
| Wait for repair (back about 14:30) | 150 | 40.5 |
| Reassign LH-11 | 180 | 27.9 |

- **Assumptions:** Each stope's hourly rate is its plan tonnes divided by the 10 h productive window. LH-11 stays at TP-1310-04 to 17:00, because LH-07 has a history of repeat hydraulic failures.
- **Confidence:** 0.7. The cause of the failure is unconfirmed (a pump, going by ear), and the pump spare stock is unknown. Whether the overdue preventive inspection will be done during this stop is also unknown.
